verdict: Tesla's revenue fell 9% to $19.3B as every factory switched over to the new Model Y, and with car prices lower too, operating profit shrank 66% to $0.4B — though the energy business kept booming.

kpis.label: Deliveries
kpis.note: down 13% YoY — the Model Y changeover cost weeks of production

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: operating cash flow of $2.2B, capex of $1.5B

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Selling and leasing cars — revenue fell 20% as deliveries dropped 13% during the Model Y changeover and average prices came down; regulatory credits rose to $595M.

segments.name: Energy generation and storage
segments.note: Megapack batteries and solar — storage deployments hit 10.4 GWh, more than double a year ago, and revenue jumped 67%.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Supercharging, repairs, insurance and used-car sales — up 15%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: AI, the Optimus robot, Cybercab and new vehicles — up 22% YoY as Tesla invests in autonomy.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling cars and running the company day to day — down 9% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring & other
opex.note: One-off costs of reshaping the business — there was no such charge a year ago.

otherDetail: Interest income of $400M, less $91M of interest expense and $119M of other expense (mostly currency losses) — a net +$190M below operating profit.
footerNote: Net income here is Tesla's total net income of $420M; $409M of it is attributable to common stockholders (the rest belongs to minority partners in subsidiaries).

takeaways.title: Deliveries fell
takeaways.text: Tesla delivered 336,681 cars, down 13% YoY, after the Model Y update shut production lines at all four vehicle factories for several weeks — and lower prices cut automotive revenue 20%.

takeaways.title: Margins squeezed hard
takeaways.text: Operating income fell 66% to $399M — a 2.1% operating margin — as lower prices and lost production overwhelmed cheaper costs per car and higher regulatory-credit sales.

takeaways.title: Energy is quietly surging
takeaways.text: Energy generation and storage revenue jumped 67% to $2.7B on record storage deployments of 10.4 GWh, and services revenue rose 15% — the non-car business kept growing through the car slump.
